_source: ~/Downloads/Next Week's Events.eml -- the DaIS edition of Thursday 24 September 2026, covering Monday 28 September to Friday 2 October. Every `theirLine` and `theirTitle` below was verified present in that file before it was written here.
_why: The engineering differential proves the simulator reproduces one publication. This one proves `purpose` carries behaviour rather than being a label: a Thursday publication covering the *following* week, a layout with no day headings, and prose attribution. If the DAIS shape were hardcoded behind a name, this fixture would be the thing that could not be made to pass.

_edition.note: No submission deadline appears anywhere in the edition -- it says only to send an email -- so the schedule declares none rather than inventing a date to put in front of an editor. The Sunday end is the one unconfirmed part: every event in the sample fell Monday to Friday, so nothing here distinguishes a Mon-Fri window from a Mon-Sun one, and including a day that should not be there is more visible than dropping one.

events.theirTitle: Emergent Symbol Processing as a Mechanistic Theory of Human Cognition

expect.why: Identical to their line, character for character -- the shared meridiem, the dropped :00, the abbreviated month, and the room split off a bare `Friend 006`.

events.theirTitle: Data-Driven Social Science Connect & Interdisciplinary Exchange
events.theirLine: 12:10 — 1:10 p.m., Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Bendheim House, 103
events.ourLine: 12:10 — 1:10 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Bendheim House 103

expect.why: The editor expanded the acronym and wrote a comma after the meridiem and before the room. We print the publisher's own title and hold one punctuation form.

events.theirTitle: DARK MANSIONS: AI, Innovation, and Fermat’s Last Theorem
events.theirLine: 12:15 — 1:15 p.m., Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Computer Science Building 105
events.ourLine: 12:15 — 1:15 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Computer Science Building 105

ourLineBySource.citp: 12:15 — 1:15 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Computer Science Building 105
ourLineBySource.dais: 12:15 — 1:15 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 29, in Computer Science 105

expect.why: Two selected sources publish it and they disagree about the venue: citp writes `Computer Science Building`, dais writes `Computer Science`. Neither is corrected. The editor credited only CITP; both rows appear here and the repeat count says so.

events.theirTitle: DaIS Launch & Faculty Research Collaboration Symposium
events.theirLine: 1— 3:45 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 30, in Frist Health Center, A78B McLain Pavillion
events.ourLine: 1 — 3:45 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 30, in Frist Health Center - A78B McLain Pavilion

expect.why: Their line has no space before the dash and misspells Pavilion. Ours reproduces the feed's own LOCATION whole: neither half of `Frist Health Center - A78B McLain Pavilion` is room-shaped, so it is left unsplit rather than guessed at.

events.theirLine: 9 - 10 a.m. Friday, Oct. 2, in Bendheim House 103
events.ourLine: 9 — 10 a.m. Friday, Oct. 2, in Bendheim House 103

expect.why: A morning range, so the shared meridiem is `a.m.` -- the case that breaks if the meridiem is taken from the start time and printed twice. Their hyphen against our em dash is the inconsistency this generates away: the same edition uses both.

events.theirLine: 1:30 — 3 p.m. Friday, Oct. 2, in Julis Romo Rabinowitz, A01
events.ourLine: 1:30 — 3 p.m. Friday, Oct. 2, in Julis Romo Rabinowitz Building A01

expect.why: The editor drops `Building` and writes a comma; we print the venue the feed names. This is the event that found the dangling separator: `Julis Romo Rabinowitz Building - A01` was splitting to a venue name ending in a bare dash.

events.theirTitle: Advancing Robotic Assembly in Construction through Learning and Adaptive Control

expect.why: In the live robotics feed, not in the committed snapshot. Recorded because it is the event that proves `location TBA`: the feed carries no location, and the DAIS template writes those words where the engineering template omits the line.

events.theirLine: 4:30 – 5:30 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026, in Sherrerd Hall, Room 101
events.ourTitle: Honeycombs and Sums of Hermitian Matrices, Revisited

expect.why: Not in the committed ORFE snapshot, as with three of the engineering edition's events. Recorded for the divergence rather than the coverage: the editor wrote the *series* name and linked the semester flyers page; the live ORFE feed carries the actual talk, by Ankur Moitra. We have better data than the edition does.

_extras.note: Two events fall in the window, declare the purpose, and are not in the edition. An editor untickng them is the designed behaviour -- the simulator offers what the feeds carry and does not decide an edition.
events: Bias in AI Reading Group (citp, Thursday 1 October) -- CITP declares the purpose and publishes more than DaIS prints.
Northeast Robotics Colloquium (robotics, Saturday 3 October) -- the one all-day event, and the reason the window's Sunday end is worth stating.

_divergences.what: Attribution verbs vary in theirs and not in ours
_divergences.theirs: Hosted by / Co-sponsored by / Presented by, chosen per event
_divergences.verdict: No feed carries a verb. Printing `Co-sponsored by` would be asserting a fact about an arrangement we cannot see.

_divergences.what: NAM's speaker does not reach the listing
_divergences.verdict: nam puts it in DESCRIPTION -- `Speaker: Taylor Webb, Department of Psychology, Princeton University` -- and nothing reads a speaker out of DESCRIPTION. SUMMARY rules and page enrichment are the two routes that exist; this is a real gap, recorded rather than papered over, and it is why the blurb is suppressed too (the content opens with a labelled field).

_divergences.what: One of their `Learn More` links points at the wrong event
_divergences.theirs: The DDSS Connect entry links to the NAM event page
_divergences.ours: every link is built from its own event's urlRef
_divergences.verdict: A transcription error in the hand-authored original, and the plainest argument for generating the thing.
